q.t: India's southernmost point is…
q.e: Indira Point in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Kanyakumari is the southern tip of the mainland.

q.t: A species found in one place and nowhere else is…
q.e: Endemic means belonging only to that one place.

q.t: The world's largest mangrove forest is…
q.e: The Sundarbans, where the Ganga meets the sea.

q.t: Coral reefs are built by…
q.e: Corals are tiny animals whose skeletons build up into reefs.

q.t: The Seven Sisters plus Sikkim make up…
q.e: These eight states form Northeast India.

q.t: Living root bridges are found in…
q.e: They are grown by training living tree roots across streams.

q.t: Silent Valley is in…
q.e: It is a rainforest saved from a dam by the Save Silent Valley Movement.

q.t: On a ferry, who should wear a life jacket?
q.e: Falling into open water is sudden, cold and rough.

q.t: The Hargila is a…
q.e: The Greater Adjutant Stork, protected by women in Assam.

q.t: Bhut Jolokia is…
o: One of the world's hottest chillies
q.e: Grown in the Northeast, it is even used to keep elephants away.

q.t: Why do tall island trees have buttress roots?
o: Soil is shallow, so they widen their base
q.e: Like card triangles on a paper tube, a wide base stops toppling.

q.t: Why do mangrove roots stick up out of the mud?
o: To take in air — the mud has almost none
q.e: Roots must breathe; these are the roots' snorkels.

q.t: Why are coral reefs so full of life?
o: They give hollows and ledges to hide, feed and breed
q.e: Like a forest on land, a reef provides structure.

q.t: Why do islands have so many endemic species?
o: They are cut off, so life changes to suit them alone
q.e: Isolation means living things can't easily leave or arrive.

q.t: Why are houses in the Northeast often on bamboo stilts?
o: People build with local materials suited to the climate
q.e: Local materials and climate shape local designs.

q.t: A biodiversity hotspot is a place…
o: Rich in species found nowhere else, and under threat
q.e: Both halves matter: rich in unique life AND threatened.

q.t: The Western Ghats run through…
o: Gujarat to Tamil Nadu on India's west side
q.e: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

q.t: Why is Silent Valley called 'silent'?
o: It lacks the constant buzzing of cicadas
People are not allowed to speak
q.e: Unlike most rainforests, cicadas don't fill it with sound.

q.t: The Apatani of Arunachal Pradesh grow…
o: Rice and fish in the same field
q.e: A clever system with no machines or fertilisers.

q.t: Protected areas are places where…
o: Trees can't be cut and animals can't be harmed
q.e: The government keeps them safe.

q.t: Why is a mangrove belt called the cheapest sea wall?
o: It tires out storm waves, repairs itself and costs nothing
q.e: Waves lose energy pushing through thousands of trunks and roots.

q.t: Why is losing an endemic species so serious?
o: It is lost from the whole world
q.e: There's no other population anywhere to replace it.

q.t: Why does a damaged reef take decades to recover?
o: It is built from skeletons of many generations of tiny animals
q.e: Reefs grow very slowly.

q.t: Why do so many rivers start in the Western Ghats?
o: High hills catch lots of rain that runs downhill
q.e: High ground catches rain, which then flows down — Chapter 1's rule.

q.t: Why do forests keep a river flowing all year?
o: Roots and leaves let water soak in and release it slowly
q.e: Strip the forest and the same rain becomes a June flood and an April dry bed.

q.t: How was the Hargila saved?
o: People came to want the bird through songs, cloth and children's help
q.e: You can't protect an animal that the people living beside it want gone.

q.t: Living root bridges are special because they…
q.e: They are grown, not built, and strengthen over years.

q.t: The Sundarbans masks worn on the back of the head are meant to…
o: Confuse tigers, which usually attack from behind
q.e: A face looking back may stop a tiger attacking.

q.t: How did people of North Sentinel Island possibly survive the 2004 tsunami?
q.e: Changes in wind, sea and animal behaviour may have warned them.

q.t: Why do classroom maps make people think Kanyakumari is India's southern tip?
o: Islands are squeezed into a box in a corner
Indira Point is in the north
q.e: Islands drawn small in a box look like an afterthought.

q.t: A paper tube topples; with card triangles glued at its base it stands. Which tree part does this model?
q.e: Widening the footing means it must lean much further to tip.

q.t: Mangroves solve two problems. One is lack of air. The other is…
q.e: Most plants can't survive salty ground; mangroves can.

q.t: The Save Silent Valley Movement showed that…
o: Ordinary people acting together can change a decision
q.e: Villagers, students, scientists and writers stopped the dam.

q.t: Why do schoolchildren help survey mangoes in the Western Ghats?
o: Local people know special trees that aren't in any book
q.e: Over 200 kinds of mango have been recorded with local help.

q.t: A place with many species but no threat is…
q.e: A hotspot must be both unusually rich AND threatened.

q.t: Which is India's hotspot?
q.e: Western Ghats, the Himalaya, the Northeast and the islands are hotspots.

q.t: Why is a life jacket important even for strong swimmers?
o: It keeps you afloat when injured, cold or panicking
q.e: Open water is nothing like a pool.

q.t: Cities far away drink water that fell on the Western Ghats. So protecting these hills…
o: Protects water for millions of people
q.e: The forest turns rain into rivers that flow all year.

q.t: The Silent Valley dam story connects to Chapter 2's dam question because…
o: Benefits and costs both were real; people argued which mattered more
q.e: It was settled in public about which mattered more.

q.t: Sangai deer live in…
q.e: The only floating national park, made of phumdis.
